title: Repair After You Lose Your Temper | Parenting Rewind
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

narration.transcript: Sometimes the direction was reasonable, but your voice became much louder than you wanted. Acting as if nothing happened can leave a child unsure, while blaming the child for your yelling shifts responsibility away from the adult choice. Pause until both of you are calmer, then return and name your action without adding an excuse. Try: I am sorry I yelled; feeling frustrated is okay, but yelling at you was not. The shoe direction still matters, and I want to try again calmly. A clear apology models responsibility without erasing the boundary; repair means owning the response and reconnecting before trying again.

claim_limits: Suggested wording is an example, not a guaranteed result.
Adapt expectations to the individual child and safety context.
